english.title: Keep food likely to support growth of pathogenic micro-organisms or formation of toxins at temp above 8°C
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) kept food, namely **(..SPECIFY FOOD..), which was likely to support the growth of pathogenic micro-organisms or the formation of toxins and with respect to which a commercial operation was being carried out at or in food premises at **(..SPECIFY LOCATION OF FOOD PREMISES..), at a temperature above 8°C
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 17(2) of, and paragraph 2 of Schedule 4 to, the Food Hygiene (Wales) Regulations 2006.

english.notes:
(i) This offence does not apply in relation to any food business operation to which Regulation 853/2004 applies or any food business operation carried out on a ship or aircraft.
(ii) This offence does not apply in relation to any food which, as part of a mail order transaction, is being conveyed to the final consumer.
(iii) See paragraph 3 of Schedule 4 to these regulations for general exemptions to this offence.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two Years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
No prosecution for an offence under these Regulations which is punishable under paragraph (2) of regulation 17 may be begun after the expiry of (a) three years from the commission of the offence; or (b) one year from its discovery by the prosecutor, whichever is the earlier.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
